questions.question: Explain how Linux differentiates access rights between file owners, groups, and others. / [CO3, CO4] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how Linux differentiates access rights between owners, groups, and others. Linux permissions are divided into:
  • • Owner (u): Creator of the file.
  • • Group (g): Members of the assigned group.
  • • Others (o): All other users. Permissions:
  • • Read (r)
  • • Write (w)
  • • Execute (x) Example:
  • -rwxr-xr--

questions.question: Compare Bourne Shell, Bash Shell and C Shell. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare Bourne Shell, Bash Shell and C Shell.
  • Feature Bourne Shell (sh) Bash Shell C Shell (csh)
  • Developer Stephen Bourne GNU Project Bill Joy
  • Syntax Simple Bourne-compatible C-like
  • Command History Limited Extensive Available
  • Aliases No Yes Yes
  • Scripting Good Excellent Moderate
  • Popularity Older systems Most widely used Academic environments
  • Conclusion: Bash is the most widely used shell due to its advanced features and compatibility.

questions.question: Explain different types of shell available in linux with their features. / [CO3, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain different types of shell available in Linux with features. Bourne Shell (sh)
  • • Original UNIX shell.
  • • Supports scripting. Bash Shell (bash)
  • • Default Linux shell.
  • • Command history, aliases, job control. C Shell (csh)
  • • C language-like syntax.
  • • Useful for interactive use. Korn Shell (ksh)
  • • Combines features of Bourne and C Shell.
  • • Efficient scripting. TC Shell (tcsh)
  • • Enhanced version of C Shell.
  • • Command completion and editing. Z Shell (zsh)
  • • Powerful customization.
  • • Advanced completion and themes.

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of managing users and groups separately in Linux. Explain how this separation improves system security and simplifies administration in multi-user environments. / [CO3, CO4] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the effectiveness of managing users and groups separately in Linux.
  • Managing users and groups separately improves:
  • Security
  • • Access control based on user roles.
  • • Restricts unauthorized access.
  • Simplified Administration
  • • Permissions can be assigned to groups rather than individual users.
  • • Easier management of large organizations.
  • Resource Sharing
  • • Group members can share files and resources efficiently.
  • Scalability
  • • New users can be added to existing groups quickly.
  • Accountability
  • • User activities can be tracked individually.
  • Conclusion: Separate management of users and groups enhances security, flexibility, scalability,
  • and administrative efficiency in multi-user Linux environments.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
